clue.text: Pick fertile quantity of land? It's seen when going to the dogs

definitions.text: It's seen when going to the dogs

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of land area, a hundred square metres

explanation.surface: A question about choosing a plot of good farmland, with a dig at things going downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going to the dogs' sounds like decline, but here it means a night at greyhound racing.
explanation.definitionFit: At a greyhound track the dogs chase a mechanical lure running on a rail, which is what this answer names.

clue.text: Involved in European party, participate in hustings?

parts.note: short for the UK Labour Party
hustings are election platforms, where candidates make speeches

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether joining a European party means taking part in election campaigning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something involved is complicated and detailed, the adjectival sense of this word.

clue.text: Correct pieces received by person making corrections

indicators.note: what is received is taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: Fragments of text are handed to a proofreader to fix.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct its errors, a close synonym used of editing.

clue.text: Often intoxicated person on drug goes the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means travelling backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

explanation.surface: A drunk who is also on drugs heads off in the wrong direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A toper is a habitual heavy drinker, someone often intoxicated.

clue.text: Overwhelmed at one's residence, with no indication of time

parts.note: being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Someone stuck at home, swamped, has lost track of the date.
explanation.definitionFit: To be inundated is to be flooded or swamped, as with requests or work.

clue.text: Dotty clergyman loves hotel around US landmark

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: love is zero, O; two of them
H is hotel in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An eccentric vicar adores the hotel he is staying in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' looks like an anagram signal, but it simply gives a synonym; everything is then reversed together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hoover Dam on the Colorado River is a famous American landmark.

clue.text: Harder to get a drug separately packaged by rights?

indicators.note: two items each wrapped up in turn are placed apart inside the surrounding letters

parts.note: R for right, plural so three of them

explanation.surface: Asking whether a drug wrapped up by rights-holders becomes harder to obtain.
explanation.walkthrough: The A and the E go into separate gaps among the three Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rarer is scarcer, so harder to come by.

clue.text: A very soft fish with small, spicy chip, maybe

explanation.surface: A soft piece of fish served with small, spicy chips.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish-and-chips picture hides golf: a chip is a short lofted shot onto the green.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a chip is one kind of shot played towards the green, an example of the answer.

clue.text: Calm piano étude's ending with A minor triad

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

indicators.note: an ending is the final part, so only the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: the A minor chord is made of the notes A, C and E

explanation.surface: A piano study ends quietly on an A minor chord.
explanation.walkthrough: A triad is a three-note chord, and spelling out the notes of A minor gives three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace is calm, a state of tranquillity and quiet.

clue.text: Somebody who's loaded dog cart that's rickety

indicators.note: something rickety is falling apart, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A dog cart piled high with goods is wobbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaded' suggests a full cart, but it means very rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocrat is a person whose power comes from wealth; loaded is slang for rich.

clue.text: Tips for the rich making some lucrative trades, each one followed by a dip

indicators.note: the tips of words are their leading ends, so only the first letter of each is used

parts.words: the rich making some lucrative trades
parts.note: opening letters of the six words
an A placed after every one of the six letters

explanation.surface: Advice for the wealthy on trading, where each deal is followed by a slump in the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' looks like financial advice and 'dip' like a market fall; in fact six first letters each take an A after them, and the dip is a food.
explanation.definitionFit: Taramasalata is a Greek spread of fish roe served as a dip with bread.

clue.text: Wild trio of Reds with love for one Democrat given a new command

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order
one thing standing for another means a single letter is swapped out

parts.note: standard abbreviation, the letter that is replaced

explanation.surface: Three wild communists, with a Democrat swapped in for love, are put under a new leader.
explanation.walkthrough: One D among the three REDs becomes O before the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Reordered here means given a fresh order, in the sense of an instruction or command.

clue.text: Bish made by bishop breaking eggs on the counter

indicators.note: counter means running against the usual direction, so the result is read backwards
breaking into something means getting inside it

explanation.surface: A clumsy bishop cracks some eggs on the kitchen counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bish' looks like short for bishop, but it is British slang for a blunder; the bishop in the wordplay is the Right Reverend.
explanation.definitionFit: Bish is informal British slang for a mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Joy when puzzling sign is grasped by an amateur cryptologist finally

indicators.note: something grasped is held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a ham is an amateur, as in radio or acting

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: An amateur codebreaker finally cracks a puzzling symbol and is delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: An aha moment is the sudden pleasure of insight that comes when a puzzle clicks.

clue.text: Short ass hosting dissolute rave, typically

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so one piece holds the other
dissolute means dissipated and loose-living, so the letters come undone into a new order

parts.note: an onager is a wild ass

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its end, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A little donkey throws a wild party, as is its habit.
explanation.walkthrough: ONAGER loses its last letter, then holds the rearranged RAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: On average means usually or as a rule, which is what typically means.

clue.text: Rough figures in cars taking big road northwards

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside

parts.note: estate cars, British for station wagons

indicators.note: in a down entry going north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the M1, Britain's major motorway, with 1 as I

explanation.surface: Traffic figures for cars heading north on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway running north from London.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimates are approximate calculations, rough figures rather than exact ones.

clue.text: Leader in daily paper showing aspiration

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper's editorial reveals its ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' suggests a newspaper editorial, which fits the surface but is only the first-letter signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is a hope or ambition, an aspiration.

clue.text: Seriously upset artillerymen retreat through part of Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: passing through something means sitting within it

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a nest is a snug retreat

explanation.surface: Gunners in disarray fall back across the fens of Cambridgeshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' reads as a verb for the soldiers but is a noun, a hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnestly means with sincere and serious intent.

clue.text: One known for laughing long and hard, at first, given answer

indicators.note: 'at first' keeps only the first letter of 'hard'

parts.note: H for hard as in pencils, placed first

explanation.surface: Someone laughs long and hard when told the solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' moves the hard letter to the front, ahead of the word for long.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena is famous for its cackling call, which sounds like laughter.

clue.text: Shorelines possibly drawn, we hear, with 1,000 boats

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

explanation.surface: A sketch of a coastline with a thousand boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' suggests a picture but means level in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidemarks are the lines left by high water, which may trace a shoreline.

clue.text: Writer of comic books that Lady Georgette's covering

parts.note: her is the pronoun for that lady

indicators.note: a covering is the outside layer, so only the outermost letters are used

parts.note: first and last letters of the name

explanation.surface: A titled woman wraps her comic books in a silky fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady Georgette' reads as one aristocrat's name, but the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: Hergé was the Belgian cartoonist who wrote and drew the Tintin comic books.

clue.text: Cons about to leave cons

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: circa, the letter that is removed

explanation.surface: Prisoners are about to walk free.
explanation.walkthrough: The two uses of cons are a verb (to swindle) and a noun (convicts).
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to swindle them, so rooks is a synonym for the verb cons.

clue.text: What drives works of philosopher suppressing large, gleeful cry

indicators.note: suppressing something holds it in, so one piece is kept inside the others

explanation.surface: A philosopher's writings stifle a loud whoop of joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a philosopher's books, but it is a factory or mill.
explanation.definitionFit: A millwheel, turned by water, powers the machinery of a mill or works.

clue.text: Leicester's wingers receiving a pass, getting instruction for players

indicators.note: receiving something takes it in, so one piece goes inside
wingers play on the flanks, so only the two outer letters are used

parts.note: first and last letters of the name

explanation.surface: Leicester City's wide men get the ball and are given orders by the coach.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture, with players and passing, hides a musical tempo marking. Leicester is an English city with a famous football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a tempo direction telling musicians to play slowly and broadly.

clue.text: Perhaps pine to hold on to last of love, as a suitor did

indicators.note: holding on to something keeps it inside

parts.note: pine is one kind of wood

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A lovesick admirer pines and clings to the last of a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like yearning, which suits the suitor, but it is a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor courts someone, and wooed is the past tense of court in that romantic sense.

clue.text: Vessel to pick up adeptly, filled with whiskey

indicators.note: something filled has contents inside it

parts.note: W is whiskey in the NATO alphabet
to master a skill is to learn it well

explanation.surface: Deftly lifting a glass full of whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' and 'whiskey' suggest a glass; the vessel is a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-master is a sailing ship with two masts, so a vessel.

clue.text: Group books tours and so on from the east

indicators.note: touring goes all round something, so one piece wraps the other
in an across entry coming from the east means reading right to left

explanation.surface: A band publishes its tour dates and more from the eastern region.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight, especially of musicians.

clue.text: Maverick canonised, say, in religious festival

indicators.note: a maverick refuses to conform, so the letters break from their order

explanation.surface: An unconventional figure made a saint, at a church festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascension Day is the Christian feast marking Christ's ascent to heaven, forty days after Easter.
